text.content:
Full Manifestation is Calling's most dramatic option: instead of a summoned creature acting alongside you, your character is replaced by one of 8 spirit bodies for the rest of the Encounter. This page covers the shared procedure every profile follows; the mechanical details (numbers, penalties, exact wording) are drafted in the project's PLAYTEST_RULES.md and CALLING_PROFILES.md source documents, and the 8 profiles themselves live in the Calling Full Manifestations compendium as NPC Actors — see "Running It as a GM" for how those get assigned to a character.

Entering

Resolve an eligible Calling card as normal, paying its own cost. After it resolves, you may pay an additional toll to transform: burn 3 more Action Dice plus Mana equal to the card's Rank + 1 (the Summoner Origin reduces the die burn to 2). Rolled dice can't also pay this burn, and a Reaction can never manifest a form. Which of the 8 bodies you can choose is gated by Calling Rank: Rank 0 offers Familiar or Sprite, Rank 1 adds Beast/Phantom/Golem, Rank 2 adds Elemental/Ancestor/Fey.

What Carries Over

You are not gaining a second creature or a fresh turn. The form replaces you in your current space and uses your turn exactly as it stood: whatever Action Dice and Reaction Dice you have left remain exactly that many, your Movement already spent this turn stays spent, and your own ongoing Wounds and Conditions are still true underneath the new body — transforming heals nothing. Your Accumulated Damage pressure (see "Damage & Wounds Across Forms") also carries over rather than resetting.

What You Can Do While Manifested

Only that profile's own 2-3 built-in maneuvers (Actions/Reactions, tagged Manifestation in the compendium so they're never confused with the 396-card catalogue) plus compatible universal Basics — not any learned card from any Style. Maneuvers use your own Calling Rank and Attribute ratings to determine dice, never a stat on the profile Actor itself; no Expertise is required and no Mastery Surge is granted. Your normal weapon and armor sit out of play and add nothing to a profile's intrinsic maneuvers.

Leaving

Burn 1 Action Die on your turn to voluntarily dismiss, returning to your own space (or the nearest legal empty one). You can't switch directly from one form into another — dismiss first, then use a later Calling card to enter something else. The first subtype you fully manifest into during an Encounter is locked in for that whole Encounter: you can dismiss and re-enter that same body as many times as you like, but you cannot rotate through different bodies in one fight.

Each profile has its own small Wound track (3-5 boxes, same Light/Light/Serious/Serious/Critical severity pattern as a character's usual 5-box track, just truncated). This track is separate from your own Core Wounds and, per the rules, persists for the entire Adventure — not just one fight. In this system that persistence is literal: the profile is a real NPC Actor, and its Wound boxes simply stay marked between sessions until Downtime treats them.

The Shared Pressure Counter

Accumulated Damage (the pressure that has to exceed Resilience before a hit becomes a real Wound) belongs to you, not to whichever body is currently active, and it does not reset just because you transformed, dismissed, or were defeated. When the next hit for amount x lands against whichever Resilience R is currently active:

new Wounds = max(0, D + x - R) - max(0, D - R)

...then D becomes D + x. This prevents switching bodies from erasing pressure you'd already built up, and prevents being charged twice for a hit you already absorbed.

Worked example: D is 2 when you enter a Golem (Resilience 2). Entry itself adds no Wound. A following hit for 1 Damage causes max(0, 3-2) - max(0, 2-2) = 1 Wound to the Golem; D becomes 3. Dismissing afterward does not reset D or undo that Wound.

Defeat

When a hit fills a profile's last Wound box, the form collapses immediately: any Wounds from that same hit beyond the track's remaining capacity transfer to you, and you additionally suffer 1 feedback Wound just from being forced out (Temporary Wounds can absorb either). You return to your own body, and that specific subtype is marked Broken until Downtime — your other subtypes remain available. No profile ability heals, restores Resources, removes a Wound, or suppresses a Critical Wound's incapacitating effect.

A profile marked Living is a valid target for a living-only effect; one marked Nonliving is not, but otherwise still feels pain, can be restrained, and is affected by mental attacks, magic, forced movement and ordinary Conditions like anything else — being a Phantom does not confer incorporeality.

These numbers are provisional playtest values, not finalized adversary statistics — compare them against your table's actual characters before treating them as settled.

The 8 profiles live pre-built in the Calling Full Manifestations compendium as NPC Actors, each already carrying its 2-3 maneuvers as owned Action/Reaction Cards — open one from the compendium to read its full stat block and maneuver text exactly like any other NPC.

Assigning a Profile to a Character

A compendium document can't hold Wounds or player ownership, so the first time a character fully manifests a given subtype, drag that profile from the compendium into the world (or duplicate it) to create that character's own persistent copy — this is what makes the Wound record actually persist across sessions, since it's just a normal world Actor that never gets deleted. Grant the controlling player Owner permission on it so they can open and act from it directly, the same as opening their own character's sheet. If that same character manifests the same subtype again later, reuse this same world copy rather than creating another one.

Swapping Control

While manifested, the simplest way to run it at the table is to swap which Actor the character's combat token represents — point the token at the profile Actor for the duration, then back at the character's own Actor on dismissal or defeat. The Combat Tracker's turn order doesn't need to change; only which sheet the player is looking at does.

Not Yet Automated

This guide documents the ruling, not a one-click tool — entering/dismissing/defeat and the Accumulated Damage carryover above are currently tracked by hand, the same way Contingency, Threads, and the other Combat Style Specialties are. Treat every number and interaction here as a provisional playtest draft, not finalized canon.
